correctness.rationale: The proof establishes a bijection between all binary order-five de Bruijn necklaces and those of the 65,536 four-suffix Boolean feedback maps whose induced 32-state permutation is a single cycle. The checker iterates every map with integer arithmetic, separately reproduces the complete 2,048-necklace set by Euler tours, and compares greedy complete-arch indices with independent earliest-embedding distinct-subsequence dynamic programming at all 32 rotations. Its exact 512/768/768 feedback table proves all class frequencies; the two relevant feedback entries exactly characterize the two circular alternating length-six factors, and both together force a prohibited 2-cycle. The complete finite proof is in RESULT.md, the executable exhaustive enumeration in checker.py. Finite claims only, no infinite inference.

value.rationale: Classical de Bruijn cycles are maximally universal for contiguous five-bit windows, but scattered-subsequence universality of a single circular traversal is a different natural invariant. The exact dichotomy, its sharp index endpoints, and the small six-letter alternating-factor obstruction give a structural recognition criterion across all 2,048 cycles instead of a list of samples. Exact per-rotation class frequencies complete this tractable order-five census and create reproducible benchmarks for subsequence-based sequence analysis. The small rank is mathematically motivated by its classical full necklace count and exhaustive feasibility. No unproved relevance to larger orders or performance application is asserted.
